applies_why: This judge text resolves the Luke 2:48-49 link by treating Mary's phrase "thy father" as immediately qualified by the child's "my Father" language, i.e., by verse-level comparison rather than by weighing the relevant chain against chain by footing.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase "never verse by verse" could forbid any verse-level qualification when the collision is between the pressing side's own chain read together, or it could forbid only an express "no contrary verse in its own words" test; the judge text uses an immediate verse-level qualification of Luke 2:48-49.
why: The judge's stated reason is a verse-level qualification of Luke 2:48 by Luke 2:49, not a chain-against-chain footing analysis as K-C requires when that rule applies.
